pullRequest.title: LEAVE-58 Let employees cancel their own time-off requests

analysis.featureSummary: LEAVE-58: employees can cancel their own Pending or Approved time-off requests in Dayoff via a Cancel button in "My requests" and POST /api/requests/:id/cancel. Cancelling sets status Cancelled; cancelling Approved leave returns its days to the balance but (per the later payroll comment, overriding the original 'any time before the first day') is only allowed when the first day is at least 3 days after today. Only the requesting employee may cancel (others get 403); cancelled requests cannot be decided (409) and appear under the manager's Decided list; repeated cancel returns 409 without refunding twice.

ambiguities.question: What HTTP status should the API return when an Approved cancel is refused because of the 3-day notice rule (409, 400, 422)?
ambiguities.why: The ticket only says the cancel is refused with a message; the PR returns 409. A tester cannot assert the status code of the notice refusal until this is decided.

ambiguities.question: Which time zone defines 'today' for the 3-day notice rule: the employee's local date, the company's time zone, or the server's UTC date?
ambiguities.why: Near midnight the date differs between zones, so the boundary case (first day = today + 3 vs today + 2) cannot be given a definite expected outcome until the reference clock is fixed.

ambiguities.question: Are the 3 days of notice calendar days, or working days (excluding weekends/holidays)?
ambiguities.why: The comment says 'today + 3' which reads as calendar days, but 'days' is used elsewhere for leave days which may be working days; boundary tests over a weekend have no defined expected result.

ambiguities.question: Should a Cancel button still be shown on an Approved request that is already inside the 3-day window (or already started/past), or should it be hidden or disabled?
ambiguities.why: The description says every Approved request has a Cancel button, while the comment makes such cancels always fail; the expected UI for in-window Approved rows cannot be asserted until clarified.

ambiguities.question: What should the API return when an employee tries to cancel another employee's request: 403 (as the ticket says) even though that reveals the request exists, or 404?
ambiguities.why: The ticket says 403 for another employee; confirming this avoids a dispute if the implementation chooses 404 to hide other people's requests.

ambiguities.question: What exact status code and message are expected when cancelling a Rejected request through the API?
ambiguities.why: The ticket only says Rejected requests have no Cancel button; it does not define the API response for a direct call, so the test can only be inferred.

ambiguities.question: Does a Cancelled request still count against overlap/duplicate checks when the employee creates a new request for the same dates?
ambiguities.why: The ticket does not say whether cancelled leave frees the dates for a new request; a tester cannot know whether re-requesting the same days should succeed.

risks.description: Off-by-one in the notice check: an Approved request starting today + 2 is allowed to be cancelled (and its days refunded), contradicting the payroll rule.
risks.basis: noticeDays() returns Math.round((start - today)/DAY) + 1 and refuses only when that is < 3. For start = today + 2 it returns 3, so the cancel succeeds; only today + 1 and earlier are refused. The comment explicitly says 'today + 2 is not' fine.

risks.description: No ownership check: any employee can cancel another employee's request, and for Approved leave the days are refunded to the owner without their action.
risks.basis: The cancel route only checks user.role !== 'employee' for 403; it finds the request by id across all requests and never compares request.employee to the signed-in user.

risks.description: Time zone mismatch on 'today': the server uses the UTC date while employees and payroll likely think in local dates, so the boundary may shift by a day near midnight.
risks.basis: noticeDays() computes today as new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10) (UTC) and Date.parse on YYYY-MM-DD (UTC midnight).

risks.description: Manager's Decided list may not show Cancelled requests (or may show them still awaiting decision) if the existing manager screen filters on Approved/Rejected or on status !== Pending in ways that were not checked.
risks.basis: The PR states the Decided list works 'without any change to that screen'; app.js manager code was not changed or shown in the diff.

risks.description: Decision endpoint behaviour for Cancelled requests is assumed, not changed: if decide() checks only for 'Approved'/'Rejected' rather than 'not Pending', a manager could approve a Cancelled request and deduct days again.
risks.basis: The PR relies on 'the decision endpoint only accepts Pending requests'; the decision code was not modified in the diff.

risks.description: Balance display may be stale after cancel if render() does not re-fetch /api/me, or the cancel error alert may persist after a later successful action.
risks.basis: The Cancel onclick calls render() after the POST; whether render re-reads the balance is not visible in the diff. cancelError is set on failure and never explicitly cleared.

risks.description: Balance consistency: double cancels, concurrent cancels, or cancel racing with a manager decision could refund days twice or leave status and balance inconsistent.
risks.basis: cancel() mutates users.balance and request.status in memory; the already-cancelled guard exists but concurrent requests and approve-vs-cancel ordering are untested.

risks.description: Refusal message wording must state the 3 days; a change to CANCEL_NOTICE_DAYS or message text could break this requirement.
risks.basis: Message is 'Approved leave can only be cancelled at least 3 days before its first day.' built from CANCEL_NOTICE_DAYS.

risks.description: Accessible name uses raw ISO dates ('Cancel request from YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD'); screen-reader tests that look for the dates as displayed must match the same format, and identical date ranges would give duplicate names.
risks.basis: ariaLabel: `Cancel request from ${request.start} to ${request.end}` in app.js.

risks.description: Pending requests whose dates are already in the past can be cancelled; also a Pending cancel must not touch the balance, which depends on balance being deducted only on approval.
risks.basis: cancel() skips the notice and balance logic entirely for Pending; correctness of R7 depends on when the existing code deducts days.

scenario.title: Employee cancels a Pending request from My requests; balance unchanged
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee. Record the number shown as Days remaining as balanceBefore. Using the Request time off form, request leave with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10 and any reason. In My requests, find the row for this new Pending request and look at its Cancel button and that button's accessible name. Click that Cancel button. Without reloading, look at the row's status and record Days remaining as balanceAfterCancel. Then reload the page and look again at the row's status, check whether the row still offers a Cancel button, and record Days remaining as balanceAfterReload.

assertions.description: Before cancelling: a Cancel button exists in the My requests row of the new Pending request (2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10).
Before cancelling: the accessible name of that row's Cancel button contains the first day 2027-03-08.
Before cancelling: the accessible name of that row's Cancel button contains the last day 2027-03-10.
After clicking Cancel and reloading: the status shown in the My requests row for 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10 contains Cancelled.
Days remaining right after the cancel (no reload), balanceAfterCancel, equals balanceBefore recorded before the request was made.
Days remaining after reload, balanceAfterReload, equals balanceBefore.
After reload: the My requests row for the now Cancelled request 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10 has no Cancel button.
Via GET /api/requests as the employee after the cancel: the status field of the request with first day 2027-03-08 equals Cancelled.

scenario.title: Employee cancels an Approved far-future request in the UI; days returned immediately and after reload
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee and request leave with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10 and any reason. Record Days remaining as balanceBeforeApproval. Sign out, sign in as the manager and approve this request. Sign out and sign in again as the employee. Record Days remaining as balanceApproved. In My requests, look at the Cancel button on the Approved row and its accessible name. Click Cancel. Without reloading, record Days remaining as balanceAfterCancel and look at the row's status. Reload the page and record Days remaining as balanceAfterReload, and look at the row's status again.

assertions.description: After approval, before cancelling: a Cancel button exists in the My requests row of the Approved request 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10.
After approval: the accessible name of that Approved row's Cancel button contains the last day 2027-03-10.
Right after clicking Cancel, without reload: the status shown in the row for 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10 contains Cancelled.
Days remaining right after the cancel without reload (balanceAfterCancel) equals balanceBeforeApproval, i.e. the request's days were returned.
Days remaining right after the cancel (balanceAfterCancel) is at least balanceApproved + 1 (the balance went up).
Days remaining after reloading the page (balanceAfterReload) equals balanceBeforeApproval.

scenario.title: Non-owner employee cannot cancel someone else's Approved request
scenario.intent: Sign in as employee owner and create a request with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10. Sign out, sign in as the manager and approve it; note the request id. Sign out and sign in as owner; record Days remaining as ownerBalanceBefore. Sign out and sign in as employee other. As other, POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel for owner's request and record the HTTP status code as otherCancelStatus. Sign out, sign in as owner, record Days remaining as ownerBalanceAfter and look at the request's status in GET /api/requests.

assertions.description: HTTP status code of other's POST /api/requests/<owner request id>/cancel (otherCancelStatus) equals 403.
After other's attempt, signed in as owner: status field of the request in GET /api/requests equals Approved.
After other's attempt: owner's Days remaining (ownerBalanceAfter) equals ownerBalanceBefore.

scenario.title: Manager cannot cancel an employee's request
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee and create a request with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10; note its id and record Days remaining as balanceBefore. Sign out, sign in as the manager and POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel; record the HTTP status code as mgrCancelStatus. Sign out, sign in as the employee, read the request's status from GET /api/requests and record Days remaining as balanceAfter.

assertions.description: HTTP status code of the manager's POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel (mgrCancelStatus) equals 403.
After the manager's attempt, as the employee: status field of the request in GET /api/requests equals Pending.
After the manager's attempt: employee's Days remaining (balanceAfter) equals balanceBefore.

scenario.title: Cancelled request leaves the manager's queue, shows under Decided and cannot be approved or rejected
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee, create a request with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10, note its id, record Days remaining as balanceBefore, and cancel it with the Cancel button in My requests. Sign out, sign in as the manager and view the main page: look for the request in the Requests awaiting a decision section and in the Decided section, and read its status in Decided. Then POST /api/requests/<id>/decision with decision approve and record the HTTP status code as approveStatus; then with decision reject and record it as rejectStatus. Sign out, sign in as the employee, read the request's status from GET /api/requests and record Days remaining as balanceAfter.

assertions.description: Manager main page after the cancel: no entry for the request 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10 is listed under Requests awaiting a decision.
Manager main page after the cancel: the entry for the request 2027-03-08 to 2027-03-10 under Decided shows a status containing Cancelled.
HTTP status code of the manager's POST /api/requests/<id>/decision with approve (approveStatus) equals 409.
HTTP status code of the manager's POST /api/requests/<id>/decision with reject (rejectStatus) equals 409.
After both decision attempts, as the employee: status field of the request in GET /api/requests equals Cancelled.
After both decision attempts: employee's Days remaining (balanceAfter) equals balanceBefore.

scenario.title: Double cancel of an Approved request via API: 409 and no second refund
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee, create a request with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10 and note its id. Sign out, sign in as the manager and approve it. Sign out, sign in as the employee and record balance from GET /api/me as balanceApproved. POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel; keep its response body and record the HTTP status. Record balance from GET /api/me as balanceAfterFirst. POST the same cancel again and record its HTTP status code as secondCancelStatus. Record balance from GET /api/me as balanceAfterSecond.

assertions.description: Response body of the first POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel: its status field equals Cancelled.
balanceAfterFirst (GET /api/me balance after the first cancel) is at least balanceApproved + 1.
HTTP status code of the second POST /api/requests/<id>/cancel (secondCancelStatus) equals 409.
balanceAfterSecond (GET /api/me balance after the second cancel) equals balanceAfterFirst.

scenario.title: Rejected request has no Cancel button while a Pending one does
scenario.intent: Sign in as the employee and create two requests: one with first day 2027-03-08, last day 2027-03-10, and one with first day 2027-04-12, last day 2027-04-14. Sign out, sign in as the manager and reject only the 2027-03-08 request. scenario.title: Pending request starting tomorrow can still be cancelled (notice rule only for Approved)
scenario.intent: Work out today's date (use the Date header of a response from the application) and let D be today + 1 day in YYYY-MM-DD. Sign in as the employee, record Days remaining as balanceBefore, create a request with first and last day D and leave it Pending. In My requests click the Cancel button of that row. assertions.description: After clicking Cancel on the Pending request starting tomorrow: status field of that request in GET /api/requests equals Cancelled.

scenario.title: Approved request starting exactly today + 3 can be cancelled (boundary)
scenario.intent: Create and approve a request whose first day is today + 3, then cancel it as the employee and check status Cancelled and days returned.

scenarios.blockedReason: The outcome at exactly today + 3 depends on whether the 3 days are calendar or working days (over a weekend they differ) and on which time zone defines today (server UTC vs local). Decide both before this boundary can be asserted.

scenario.title: HTTP status of a notice-window refusal
scenario.intent: Cancel an Approved request starting tomorrow via the API and check the HTTP status code of the refusal.

scenarios.blockedReason: The ticket only says the cancel is refused with a message; the expected status code (409, 400 or 422) is not documented.

scenario.title: Cancel button and UI error for an Approved request inside the notice window
scenario.intent: With an Approved request starting tomorrow, check in My requests whether a Cancel button is offered and, if clicked, that the refusal message is shown on screen and the row stays Approved.

scenarios.blockedReason: The description says every Approved request has a Cancel button, while the payroll rule makes in-window cancels always fail; it must be decided whether the button is shown, hidden or disabled for such rows before the UI can be asserted.

scenario.title: Cancelling a Rejected request through the API
scenario.intent: Create and reject a request, then POST the cancel endpoint directly and check the response, status and balance.

scenarios.blockedReason: Only an inferred requirement covers a direct API cancel of a Rejected request; the expected status code and outcome are not documented.

scenario.title: Re-requesting the same dates after cancelling
scenario.intent: Cancel a request, then submit a new request for the same dates and check whether it is accepted.

scenarios.blockedReason: It is not documented whether a Cancelled request still counts in overlap or duplicate checks for a new request on the same dates.

scenario.title: Unauthenticated cancel and cancel of a non-existent id
scenario.intent: Call the cancel endpoint without a session and with an unknown request id, and check the responses and that nothing changes.

scenarios.blockedReason: The 401 and 404 responses are inferred requirements only; the documentation does not state the expected codes. Confirm them before asserting.
